Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with lumbar back strain. The reported mechanism of injury is
consistent with the forces expected in a collision of this type. Over the cuorse of 22 visits, the patient received manual therapy,
therapeutic exercise, and home exercise instruction, with visit frequency decreasing steadily as symptoms improved and the care
plan moved toward discharge. Examination findings included paraspinal muscle tenderness and reduced lumbar range of motion,
which support the reported injury, while neurological screening and straight-leg raise testing were within normal limits. The
patient reports a remote, small strain to the same area in the past that resolved completely without lasting limitation. Treatment
was delivered in a standard, non-repetitive pattern, and the patient was discharged with a self-management plan and instructions
to return if symptoms recur.
